correctness.rationale: For m=b²+b+1 and arbitrary b≥2, b³≡1 mod m groups arbitrary numeral digits by exponents modulo 3. Conversely each nonnegative (A,B,C) is realized by disjoint digit-one powers of b, proving no finite-length restriction. Three seed triples produce weighted sum m and digit sums 3,b+2,2b+1. For s≤2b+1 subtract min(A,B,C) and cyclically rotate to C=0; then 0<A+bB<2m and divisibility forces A+bB=m. Integer inequalities give B∈{b,b+1}, hence no smaller unexpected weights. Beyond 2b+1 residue representatives supply all positive members of semigroup <3,b+2,2b+1>. For b≡1 mod3 only positive multiples 3 occur; otherwise Apery set {0,b+2,2b+1} gives Frobenius 2b−2, conductor 2b−1 and genus b. Independent brute force checked 528 finite (base,weight) cases via residue-zero three-count enumeration, not an infinite proof.
residual_risks: Frobenius number and genus formulas are only asserted when b is not congruent to 1 mod 3; infinite gaps otherwise.
Sufficiency depends on placing exactly A,B,C distinct powers rather than treating weighted sum A+bB+b²C as the literal base-b numeral.
